summary: conv-context-next preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: Package's preinstall script (`node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun runtime (bun-v1.3.13) from GitHub, extracts and chmods it in a temp directory, then invokes it via execFileSync against a bundled 727KB obfuscated JavaScript file `math_init.js`. The payload is a Bun-CJS bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) that uses string-array rotation obfuscation (`WV8StW` rotator over a >1500-entry constant table). This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: the obfuscated payload is executed under a freshly-downloaded alien runtime at npm install time, evading Node-based static analysis. The package advertises itself as a conversation-context library (README shows `require('conv-context')`), and the name `conv-context-next` aligns with an unrelated legitimate package — a lookalike shape unrelated to the shipped dropper. Installing the package causes arbitrary attacker-controlled code to execute on the installer's machine before any application code runs.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
